title: The millionaire's daughter who wanted to marry Blanton
summary: A wealthy Los Angeles man offered Blanton a life of ease; Blanton refused to give up the bass.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

I remember -- I told you about that, the guys who tried to get him away from us in California, Wanted to marry his daughter.
No, you didn't tell me about that.

No? Man, this guy in California -- this thing isn't running, is it? I'll tell it to you. This guy in California, a very wealthy man, and he had a daughter, only child. She saw Jimmy at the Million Dollar Theater in L.A. Fell madly in love with him. Beautiful kid. And she told her father, he'd give her anything in the world she wants. She said, 'I want to marry him.' He said, 'If that's what you want, all right.'
He came and seen us and he was amazed at Jimmy, a fine looking kid and could play. So he comes and asks Jimmy out to dinner and things. And he told Jimmy, 'My daughter loves you. If you marry my daughter you'll never have to play this bass again in your life.' A millionaire, man. I'll put you in any kind of business you want, set you up for life.'
(Laughter)
Jimmy looked at the man and he said, 'No, I would never be happy if I couldn't play my bass.' He told me and Ben Webster that and we was looking at this beautiful kid, beautiful girl. And we said, 'Man, you must be stone crazy.' We and Ben told him, man, you must be losing your mind. You'd rather play the bass then live a life of ease? He say, 'I just love

playing." And that was it.
I said, "Man, find out if she's got a cousin."
